answers.answer: A need is something essential for basic living or an important responsibility, such as food, housing, education or necessary transport.
A want is something useful or enjoyable but not essential right now, such as extra shopping, premium entertainment or an impulse purchase.
Start with an amount you can repeat consistently. The 50/30/20 guide uses 20% of income for savings, but your real amount should fit your income, expenses and goals.
The 50/30/20 guide divides income into 50% needs, 30% wants and 20% savings. Treat it as an educational starting point, not a strict rule.
A budget is a plan for where your money should go before you spend it. Start with income, essential expenses, flexible spending and savings.
Track your expenses regularly. Group them by category, compare them with your income, and look for spending that can be reduced without affecting essential needs.
Set a target amount, record what you already have, choose a monthly saving amount, and check your progress every month.
Common money mistakes include spending without a plan, impulse buying, ignoring small expenses, and not keeping an emergency fund.
